notifications.howTo.generic: Send two headers with every delivery: X-Webhook-Timestamp (unix seconds) and X-Webhook-Signature (sha256= followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp + "." + body, keyed with the secret). Deliveries more than 5 minutes old are refused, so a captured one can't be replayed.
notifications.howTo.github: In GitHub, open Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook. Payload URL: the URL above. Content type: application/json. Secret: the secret above. GitHub signs each delivery (X-Hub-Signature-256).
notifications.howTo.sentry: In Sentry, open Settings → Developer Settings → Custom Integrations → Create New Integration → Internal Integration. Webhook URL: the URL above. Turn on Alert Rule Action and subscribe to Issue. Save it, then paste its Client Secret below. Sentry signs each delivery with it (Sentry-Hook-Signature).

notifications.legacySigningHint: This source predates timestamped signing and still accepts a signature over the body alone, which a captured delivery can repeat.

notifications.noLegacyDelivery: No legacy-signed delivery since the change.
notifications.switchSigningBody: From now on every delivery must send X-Webhook-Timestamp and sign timestamp + "." + body. A sender still signing the body alone will be refused. This can't be switched back.
notifications.switchSigningBodyPlatform: From now on only the platform's own signature is accepted, not the old X-Webhook-Signature header. This can't be switched back.

channels.workflow.repliesOn: Replies through this network's reply preset are now allowed (each still needs confirmation).
channels.workflow.repliesOff: Replies through this network are now off.
channels.workflow.noWorkflow: No workflow set yet — messages will not be pushed until one is.

automation.timezoneHint: The time is read in this zone, so it stays right when the clocks change.

automation.workflowStepsHint: A JSON array of steps. Write {{name}} anywhere a value should be supplied when it runs.
automation.secretParamsHint: Comma separated. A secret value is typed hidden and is redacted from the run record.
automation.deleteWorkflowBody: {name} is removed. Runs it already produced stay.

campaigns.whatsappBodyHint: Plain text. A line telling people how to stop (reply STOP) is added to every message automatically.
campaigns.reachable: This broadcast would reach {count} contacts on WhatsApp right now.
campaigns.reachableRule: Only contacts on the list who haven't unsubscribed, opted in to WhatsApp themselves, haven't replied STOP, and have a phone number. Being on the list is not WhatsApp consent.
campaigns.reachableError: Couldn't count who this would reach.
campaigns.whatsappMissing: No WhatsApp number is linked to this workspace, so a WhatsApp campaign can't be sent yet. Drafts can be saved meanwhile.
campaigns.whatsappMissingMember: No WhatsApp number is linked to this workspace yet; ask a manager to link one before sending.
campaigns.sendBodyWhatsApp: "{subject}" goes on WhatsApp to the {count} contacts on {list} who opted in to WhatsApp. Messages are paced, and each one tells people how to stop. This can't be undone.
campaigns.sendNobodyWhatsApp: Nobody on {list} can be reached on WhatsApp yet: no one there has opted in to WhatsApp with a phone number. Record opt-ins on the Contacts page first.
contacts.waOptInBody: Only do this if {who} agreed to receive WhatsApp messages from you. Joining a mailing list is not that agreement.
contacts.waOptInNoPhone: They have no phone number yet, so broadcasts won't reach them until one is added.
contacts.waReverseBody: {who} replied STOP and asked not to receive WhatsApp messages. Reverse it only if they have since asked, themselves, to be messaged again. They will be back in WhatsApp broadcasts.
contacts.waReverseConfirm: Yes, they asked to be let back in
contacts.waReversed: STOP reversed — they can receive WhatsApp broadcasts again
contactWa.title: WhatsApp {who}
contactWa.hintNew: They have no WhatsApp conversation with you yet, so you will be asked to confirm before this first message goes. Their answer arrives in the inbox.
contactWa.hintThread: This continues their WhatsApp conversation in the inbox.
contactWa.placeholder: Write the message exactly as they will read it
contactWa.pacing: Sent from the workspace's number, paced with its other messages and logged.
contactWa.confirmBody: This is the first message from the workspace's number to them. They agreed to WhatsApp messages; send only what they would expect to receive.
contactWa.reason.not_opted_in: They have not opted in to WhatsApp messages. Email consent is not WhatsApp consent: record their opt-in only if they agreed.
contactWa.reason.opted_out: They replied STOP, so no WhatsApp message can be sent to them.
contactWa.reason.no_phone: They have no usable phone number. Add one with the country code.
contactWa.reason.not_linked: This workspace's WhatsApp number is not connected.
contactWa.reason.unavailable: WhatsApp is not available on this deployment.
contactWa.reason.limit: The WhatsApp message limit for this contact has been reached.

forms.dialogHint: Choose which list it fills and which websites may use it.
forms.name: Name
forms.allowedOriginsHint: One origin per line, e.g. https://example.com. Only pages on these origins can submit the form.
forms.noOrigins: No websites allowed: while this is empty, no site can submit this form.
forms.noOriginsShort: None — no site can submit this form
forms.thanksHint: Shown to the visitor after they submit. Leave empty for the default, which tells them to confirm by email when the list uses double opt-in.
forms.embedHint: Paste this into a page on one of the allowed websites. WhatsApp consent is its own unticked box and is only sent with a phone number.
forms.disabledToast: Form turned off — submissions are refused
forms.deleteBody: "{name}" stops working on every site it's embedded on. Subscribers it already added stay on their list.
forms.emptyBody: Create one, then paste its embed code into your website.
editor.heading: Heading
campaigns.editHint: Change anything until it's sent. Once sending starts, the campaign is fixed.
campaigns.editLocked: This campaign is now “{status}”, so it can no longer be edited.
campaigns.previewEmailHint: Exactly the email recipients get, unsubscribe footer included.
campaigns.previewWhatsAppHint: Exactly the message contacts get, with the stop line added to every broadcast.
campaigns.previewEmpty: Write something to see the preview.
campaigns.testEmailHint: One copy, with [TEST] before the subject. Its unsubscribe link is a placeholder.
campaigns.testWhatsAppHint: The message goes to this workspace's own linked WhatsApp number (your "Message yourself" chat), exactly as contacts will get it. Tests never go to another number.
campaigns.testUnsaved: A test sends the saved version. Save your changes first.
campaigns.testNotASend: A test isn't a send: the campaign stays a draft and its numbers don't change. Up to 10 tests an hour per campaign.
campaigns.testNeedsSmtp: Test emails need an SMTP service for this workspace.
campaigns.testNeedsWhatsApp: A WhatsApp test needs this workspace's number linked first; see above.
research.hint: Ask the open web a question, or give it pages to read. Moharrik reads them, keeps every source, and pulls out the evidence: the sentences that matter, the companies they name, and what those companies are doing.
research.capNoSearch: Web search isn't set up on this deployment, so research can't search the web. You can still give it pages to read if a page reader is set up. Past runs are listed below.
research.capNoRead: Pages aren't opened on this deployment: a run lists what the search found, with each result's snippet.
research.capNoModel: No model is configured on this deployment, so answers aren't summarised and evidence is picked from the pages word for word. Every quote is the page's own sentence, with its link.
research.askPlaceholder: e.g. What changed in the EU AI Act for small companies this year?
research.askHint: In your own words. One run at a time per workspace; a run takes a minute or two.
research.started: Research started. This page follows it as it goes.
research.busy: A run is already going in this workspace. Only one runs at a time.
research.liveTitle: A run is already going. Only one runs at a time, so a new question waits until it finishes or is stopped.
research.emptyBody: Ask a question above. Every page the search finds is kept here with its link, whether or not it could be read.
research.progressSearching: Searching the web and opening the first result…
research.progressReading: Reading the pages: {checked} checked, {read} read so far…
research.progressHint: Sources appear below as each page is opened. You can leave this page; the run carries on.
research.cancelledBody: It was not summarised. The sources collected before it stopped are below.
research.cancelledEmpty: It stopped before any source was collected.
research.nothingFound: The search found nothing for this question.
research.answerBy: Written by {model} from the sources below, and only those. The numbers link to them.
research.answerFrom: Written from the sources below, and only those. The numbers link to them.
research.noModelBody: No model is configured on this deployment, so there is no written answer. The sources this run collected are below: follow a link, or open the text of a page that was read.
research.notSummarisedBody: The sources were collected, but no answer could be written from them. The reason:
research.sourcesHint: Every result the search returned, in its rank order. The top ones are opened and read; the rest stand on their snippet.
research.notOpened: Not opened: only the top results are read. This one stands on its snippet.
research.textEmpty: The page was read but no text was kept.
forms.readOnly: Only managers and above can create and change website forms.
forms.needList: To add a subscribe form, create a list on the Contacts page first.
forms.dialogHintInquiry: Visitors send their name, email, phone, company and a message. Each one becomes a lead, with the campaign, referrer and landing page it came from.
forms.thanksHintInquiry: Shown to the visitor after they send. Leave empty for the default, which says the message arrived and you will be in touch.
forms.embedHintInquiry: Paste this into a page on one of the allowed websites. It remembers the UTM parameters, gclid, referrer and landing page of the visit, and sends them with the message. A hidden field catches bots.
forms.deleteBodyInquiry: "{name}" stops working on every site it's embedded on. Leads it already filed stay on the Leads page.

leads.emptyBodyMember: Leads arrive here when a manager puts an inquiry form on your website.
leads.notFoundBody: It may have been in another workspace, or the link is wrong.
leads.noAttribution: Nothing recorded: the visitor came straight to the site, or the form was embedded without the snippet's attribution.
leads.convertedWithCompany: Contact, company ({company}) and deal are ready, with the message on the timeline.
leads.convertedFreeMail: Contact and deal are ready. No company: the address is free mail.
leads.spamNoConvert: Marked as spam — change the status to convert it.

integrations.notConfigured: Google is not configured on this server yet.

integrations.noneBody: Connect one above for the product you want.

integrations.product.search_console.hint: Search performance for this account's sites, and submitting sitemaps.

integrations.revenue: Also include revenue reports (for a monetised channel)

integrations.disconnected: Disconnected, and access revoked at Google.
integrations.disconnectedShared: Removed from this workspace. The same Google account is still connected elsewhere in Moharrik, so its access was not revoked at Google.
integrations.disconnectedNoRevoke: Removed from this workspace, but Google did not confirm the revoke. Remove Moharrik at myaccount.google.com/permissions to be sure.
integrations.statusReauthHint: Google no longer accepts this connection (access removed, or the password changed).
integrations.result.cancelled: The connection was cancelled at Google. Nothing was changed.

integrations.result.state: That sign-in attempt expired or was already used. Start the connect again from this page.
integrations.result.forbidden: Only an owner or admin of this workspace can connect Google accounts.
integrations.result.failed: Google could not be connected. Try again, and if it keeps failing, report it.
integrations.result.no_refresh: Google did not grant lasting access, so nothing was connected. Try again and approve the request.

integrations.result.no_identity: Google did not say which account this is, so nothing was connected. Try again.
integrations.result.not_configured: Google is not configured on this server yet.
ga4conv.title: GA4 conversions
ga4conv.hint: Send this workspace's funnel to your own Google Analytics 4 property: every new website lead, every lead you qualify or convert, and every deal you win, as GA4 events from the server (the Measurement Protocol). The embed snippets can also carry the GA4 tag, under Consent Mode. No Google sign-in is needed for this.
ga4conv.pickStream: Web stream from your GA4 property
ga4conv.pickStreamHint: Read through the Google account connected above. Choosing one fills in its measurement ID.
ga4conv.measurementIdHint: The web stream's ID, like G-ABC123XYZ. In GA4: Admin → Data streams → your website.
ga4conv.apiSecretHint: In GA4: Admin → Data streams → your website → Measurement Protocol API secrets → Create. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
ga4conv.secretStored: Stored. Type a new one to replace it.
ga4conv.secretRemoved: API secret removed, and sending switched off
ga4conv.sendEventsHint: Needs the measurement ID and the API secret. Only moments after you switch this on are sent.
ga4conv.tag: Add the GA4 tag to the embed snippets
ga4conv.tagHint: The subscribe and inquiry snippets load GA4 with everything denied until your cookie banner grants it (Consent Mode v2). Paste the snippets again after changing this.
ga4conv.debugHint: While you check the setup: events show up in GA4 under Admin → DebugView. Switch it off afterwards.
ga4conv.testNeeds: Save the measurement ID and the API secret to send a test event.
ga4conv.testSent: GA4's validation server accepted the event, and it was sent. It shows up in GA4 under Admin → DebugView as moharrik_test within a minute.
ga4conv.testInvalid: GA4's validation server refused the test event:
ga4conv.testNotSent: The event is valid, but it could not be sent:
ga4conv.whatIsSentHint: GA4's own lead-generation event names where one exists. Mark the ones that count for you as key events in GA4 (Admin → Events). No name, email, phone, company or message is ever sent.
ga4conv.when.lead_created: A website inquiry files a new lead
ga4conv.when.lead_converted: A lead is converted to a contact and a deal (with the deal's value)
ga4conv.when.deal_won: A deal moves to a won stage (with its value)
ga4conv.recentEmpty: Nothing sent yet. Events appear here as leads and deals move.

waNotify.notLinked: This workspace has no connected WhatsApp number to send notifications from.

waNotify.verified: Number verified — WhatsApp notifications are on

automation.ext.title: Install the browser extension
automation.ext.hint: The extension is how a browser you use is paired with this workspace and driven through the steps you approve, on the sites you allow.
automation.ext.name: Moharrik extension {version}
automation.ext.devBody: This build pairs with {site}, a development server. Production builds are offered by the production site.
automation.ext.checksumHint: To check the download matches, run one of these where you saved it:
automation.ext.installHint: It is not in the Chrome Web Store, so it is loaded as an unpacked extension. This takes a minute, once.
automation.ext.s1Title: Unzip it into a folder you will keep
automation.ext.s1Body: Chrome loads the extension from that folder every time it starts. Deleting or moving the folder removes the extension.
automation.ext.s2Body: Paste this into the address bar. Browsers do not let a website link to it.
automation.ext.s2Other: In Edge it is edge://extensions, in Brave brave://extensions.
automation.ext.s3Body: The switch is in the corner of the extensions page. It only allows loading an unpacked extension; it changes nothing else.
automation.ext.s4Title: Press "Load unpacked" and choose the folder
automation.ext.s4Body: Choose the folder that has manifest.json in it. Moharrik appears in the list with its version.
automation.ext.s5Body: Open the puzzle-piece menu next to the address bar and pin Moharrik, so its button is always one click away.
automation.ext.pairHint: Connecting gives this browser its own token. An admin approves it on this site, in a page the extension opens — nothing is copied between screens.
automation.ext.s6Title: Press “Connect to the site” in the extension
automation.ext.s6Body: Click the Moharrik button next to the address bar, then “Connect to the site”. Chrome asks to let Moharrik use websites: allow it, and every site you add on this page works straight away. It then opens an approval page on this site in a new tab.
automation.ext.s7Body: On that page, choose this workspace, name the browser, list the sites it may be driven on, and press Approve. The extension picks up its token by itself.
automation.ext.s7AskAdmin: Only an admin of this workspace can approve a browser. Ask one to press “Connect to the site” in the extension on that browser.
automation.ext.seeBrowsers: See them on the Automation page
automation.ext.updateBody: The extension checks for a new version when it connects and every six hours. When one is out, its button shows NEW and its window offers the download: unzip it over the same folder and press the reload arrow on Moharrik's card in the extensions page. It stays connected. A browser on an older version is also flagged on the Automation page.
automation.sched.needBrowserTitle: A schedule needs a paired browser
automation.sched.needBrowserBody: Schedules run in a browser paired with this workspace, and none is paired yet. Install the extension and pair a browser first.
trends.summary.extractive: An excerpt from the coverage itself; no model wrote it.
trends.summary.headlines: The story as the other outlets headlined it.
trends.summary.model: Summarised by {model} from the headlines and excerpts.
trends.summary.none: One headline with no excerpt: the headline is the story so far.
trends.budgetHint: Every read, scheduled or by hand, spends one. When today's budget is spent, sources wait until tomorrow (UTC).
trends.budgetScheduled: Your schedules ask for {n} a day.
trends.budgetShort: Your schedules ask for more than the budget, so some sources will wait until tomorrow.

trends.fetchedOverBudget: Today's collection budget is spent. Raise it, or the source is read again tomorrow.
trends.editTopicHint: Items are relabelled and every recent story is rescored.

automation.editor.continueOnError: Carry on if this step fails
automation.editor.unsaved: You have changes that are not saved yet.

automation.editor.created: The workflow was saved as v1.

automation.connect.checkCode: Check this code matches the extension
automation.connect.claimsHint: This is what the browser says about itself; none of it is verified. The request expires {date}.
automation.connect.workspaceHint: The browser answers to this workspace only. Its admins can rename it, change its sites or revoke it.
automation.connect.workspaceHintSome: Only the workspaces where you are an admin are listed. The browser answers to the one you choose.
automation.connect.name: Name this browser
automation.connect.hostsHint: The sites it may be driven on, comma separated. A site also allows its subdomains. Leave it empty and it can go nowhere until you add some.
automation.connect.doneReplaced: {name} was already connected to {workspace}. It has a new token now, and the old one stopped working.
automation.connect.closeTab: You can close this tab. The extension picks up its connection by itself within a few seconds.
automation.connect.noSitesYet: It may not go anywhere yet: add its sites on the Automation page.
automation.connect.refusedBody: The extension was told. Nothing was connected.
automation.connect.notFoundBody: No browser is waiting with this code. Press “Connect to the site” in the extension again for a new one.

automation.connect.noWorkspaceBody: You are not in any workspace yet. Create one, then press “Connect to the site” in the extension again.
automation.connect.signInFirst: Sign in to decide whether this browser may connect to one of your workspaces.

overview.trafficPending: Not fetched from Google Analytics yet.
gsc.hint: How your site shows up in Google Search: clicks, impressions, click-through rate and position.
gsc.importing: The first import from Search Console is running. The newest days arrive first; this page fills in as they do.
gsc.notImported: Nothing has been imported from Search Console yet.
gsc.emptyTitle: No search data in this window

gsc.emptyFiltered: Nothing matches these filters in this window.
gsc.lag: Search Console data arrives two to three days late
gsc.basisQueries: Filtered by query or page: these totals add up the queries Google names, and leave out the anonymised ones, so they are lower than the site's totals.
gsc.truncated: {n} busy days had more query rows than one import keeps; their totals are complete, their query lists are the top rows only.
gsc.positionNote: Lower is better: position 1 is the top of the results, so the axis runs downwards.
overview.searchPending: Not imported from Search Console yet.
gsc.missing: {n} days of this window are not imported yet, so these totals are partial.
gsc.prevMissing: The period before is still being imported ({n} days to go), so nothing is compared yet.

yt.hint: Your channel as YouTube reports it: every upload, and what viewers are saying.
yt.firstSync: Reading the channel from YouTube for the first time. The uploads appear in a moment.
yt.notSynced: The channel has not been read from YouTube yet.
yt.quota: YouTube quota today: {used} of {limit} units for this workspace · {all} of {allLimit} for all of Moharrik. It resets at midnight Pacific time.
yt.noVideosBody: This channel has not uploaded any videos.
yt.commentsDisabled: Comments are turned off for this video.
overview.noChartData: No data in this window yet.

yta.pending: YouTube publishes each day's numbers a day or two late; the last {n} days are not in yet and are left as a gap.
yta.emptyBody: YouTube Analytics has nothing for this window yet. A new channel or video takes a couple of days to show numbers.
yt.youtubeCounts: YouTube's counter says {n}; {p} of these are public

gsci.hint: Ask Google how it sees one page of {site}: whether it is indexed, when it was last crawled, and which canonical Google chose.
gsci.managerOnly: A manager or above of this workspace can do this.
gsci.quota: {used} of {limit} inspections used today for this site (Google's daily budget per site, shared by every workspace that reads it).
gsci.noneBody: Paste a page's address above to see how Google sees it.
gscs.hint: The sitemaps Google knows for this site, read from Google now. Submitting one asks Google to read it (again).
gscs.submitted: Sent to Google. It reads the sitemap in its own time.

ytr.hint: YouTube Reporting's daily CSV reports for this channel: channel totals, traffic sources, and devices. Google keeps them 60 days; Moharrik keeps a copy.
ytr.noJobs: This channel has no report jobs yet.
ytr.notChecked: Not checked with YouTube yet: this happens with the channel's next sync.
ytr.jobWaiting: Job created {when}. YouTube publishes the first reports about two days after a job is created.
automation.sched.secretKeep: A value is saved and sealed. Leave this blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
automation.sched.ownSteps: This schedule runs its own steps rather than a saved workflow, so only its name, browser and time can change here.

oauth.title: Connect an app to Moharrik
oauth.hint: An app is asking to use Moharrik on your behalf. It gets one workspace and only the scopes you approve here.
oauth.signInFirst: Sign in to Moharrik to choose what this app may do. You'll come straight back here.
oauth.wantsAccess: {client} wants to act in one of your workspaces
oauth.claimsHint: The app named itself. Approve only if you just asked {host} to connect to Moharrik.
oauth.loopbackHint: This app runs on your own computer (it returns to a local address). Approve only if you just started it.
oauth.noWorkspaceTitle: You're not in a workspace yet
oauth.noWorkspaceBody: An app connects to one workspace. Create one, or accept an invitation, then come back to this page.
oauth.workspaceHint: The app sees this workspace only. Connect it again to use another.
oauth.scopesHint: Untick anything it should not do. It never gets more than your role in this workspace allows.
oauth.boundHint: Its access lasts {hours} hour at a time and renews while you stay a member. Disconnect it any time in Settings → MCP tokens.
oauth.badRequestTitle: This connection request can't be used
oauth.error.invalid_client: The app isn't registered with Moharrik, or its registration couldn't be read.
oauth.error.invalid_request: The app sent an incomplete or unsafe request.
oauth.error.invalid_scope: The app asked for a permission Moharrik doesn't have.
oauth.error.invalid_target: The app asked for a different server.
oauth.error.unsupported_response_type: The app asked to sign in in a way Moharrik doesn't support.

oauth.apps.title: Connected apps
oauth.apps.hint: Apps you signed into this workspace over OAuth, such as claude.ai or ChatGPT. Each sees this workspace only.
oauth.apps.hintAll: Every app a member signed into this workspace over OAuth, such as claude.ai or ChatGPT. As an owner or admin you can disconnect any of them.
oauth.apps.emptyBody: Add Moharrik as a connector in claude.ai or ChatGPT (steps below) and it shows up here.
oauth.apps.disconnectBody: {name} loses access to this workspace immediately. It has to be approved again to reconnect.
audit.title: Audit log
audit.hint: Every change in this workspace — by a member, an MCP token, a connected app or an agent — with who, when, from where, and what changed. Secrets and message bodies are never recorded.
audit.adminOnly: The audit log is for the workspace's owners and admins.
audit.noMatchBody: Widen the dates or clear a filter.
audit.emptyBody: Changes made from now on appear here.
audit.retentionHint: Entries are kept for {days} days, then deleted.
reports.title: Reports
reports.hint: Pipeline value, win rate, conversion between stages, wins and losses over time, where leads come from and how fast the inbox answers.
reports.noAccess: Your role cannot read the CRM, so there is no report to show.
reports.customHint: Days in the workspace's time zone, up to two years.
reports.otherCurrencyClosed: {n} closed deals in another currency are counted but left out of the values, which are in {currency} only.
reports.otherCurrencyOpen: {n} open deals in another currency are counted but left out of the values ({currency} only).
reports.pipelineNow: Open deals right now, whatever the range.
reports.conversionNote: The {n} deals opened in this range, by the furthest stage each has reached ({lost} lost since). A won deal has passed every stage.
reports.noOpened: No deals opened in this range yet.
reports.bucket.day: Per day, by the day each deal closed.
reports.bucket.week: Per week (Monday to Sunday), by the day each deal closed.
reports.bucket.month: Per month, by the day each deal closed.
reports.noClosed: No deals were won or lost in this range yet.
reports.leadSourcesNote: {n} leads from website forms in this range, {converted} converted. {spam} marked spam are left out.
reports.noLeads: No leads in this range yet.
reports.inboxNote: Conversations started in this range: from the customer's first message to the team's first reply.
reports.awaitingNote: Not answered yet, so not averaged in
reports.noConversations: No conversations started in this range yet.
reports.method: Every figure is counted from the workspace's own records when the page loads. A deal counts as won or lost on the day it closed; the funnel reads each deal's stage history. Money is summed in the workspace's currency only; nothing is converted or estimated.
deals.closedOnHint: Reports count this deal as won or lost on this day.
lifecycle.label: Lifecycle stage
lifecycle.hint: Moves forward on its own when they confirm a subscription, a lead is converted, a deal is opened or won. You can set it by hand in any direction.
icp.title: Ideal customer profile
icp.hint: Who you sell to and what says a contact is warming up. Every contact and company is scored against it, 0 to 100, with the reasons shown.
icp.readOnly: Only managers and above can change the profile. This is how it is set now.
icp.defaults: The default profile is in use: only the signals are weighted until you add who fits.
icp.fitHint: Judged on the contact's company (and, for keywords, their title and tags). Leave a criterion empty to not score it.
icp.crit.industriesHint: Separate with commas. A company matches when its industry contains one of these, or the other way round.
icp.crit.sizesHint: Employees, as recorded on the company.
icp.crit.regionsPlaceholder: Egypt, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates
icp.crit.keywordsHint: Looked for in the contact's title and tags and the company's name, industry and notes. Two found is a full match.
icp.signalsHint: What your own records say they have done. 0 turns a signal off; below 0 makes it a penalty.
icp.formula: Score = the sum of weight × how much of each criterion is present, divided by the sum of the positive weights, from 0 to 100. Weights run from -10 to 10.
icp.weightRange: Every weight is a number from -10 to 10.
icp.saved: Profile saved. Every contact and company is rescored.
icp.rankingHint: The contacts list sorted by score. Open a score to see why.
icp.scoreHow: Each line is weight × how much of it holds; the score is their sum over the positive weights.
icp.companyHow: The company's own industry, size, country and notes, and what its people and deals have done.
icp.noReasons: Nothing in the profile could be judged for this record.
icp.signal.open_deal.hint: An open deal with them or their company
icp.signal.won_deal.hint: A won deal with them or their company: already a customer
icp.signal.lost_deal.hint: A lost deal with them or their company — weigh it below 0 to make it a penalty
icp.signal.inbound_lead.hint: Sent an inquiry from your website that was converted
icp.signal.inbound_lead.yes: Came in through a website form
icp.signal.inbound_lead.no: Did not come in through a form
icp.signal.conversation.hint: A chat, email or WhatsApp conversation is linked to them
icp.signal.conversation.no: Has not written to the inbox
icp.signal.subscribed.hint: Confirmed on at least one mailing list
icp.signal.whatsapp_opt_in.hint: Agreed to WhatsApp messages and has not said STOP
icp.signal.whatsapp_opt_in.no: Has not opted in to WhatsApp
icp.signal.recent_activity.hint: A note, call, meeting or task in the last 30 days
canvas.layoutSaved: Layout saved. Nothing that runs changed, so no new version.
canvas.triggerSub: How this workflow starts, and what it asks for
canvas.start.manualHint: Test it here, or run it from the workflows list with your own values.
canvas.start.noSchedules: No schedule runs this workflow yet.
canvas.start.saveFirst: Save the workflow first; a schedule runs a saved one.
canvas.start.manageSchedules: Schedules are managed on the Automation page
canvas.start.mcpHint: An assistant with this workspace's MCP token can run it by name.
canvas.paramsHint: Each {{placeholder}} in the steps is a value the run asks for.
canvas.testValuesHint: Used when you press Test workflow. They are not saved with the workflow.
canvas.insertHere: Add a step here, as step {n}
canvas.emptyHint: Start with the + : most workflows open a page first.
canvas.needValues: This run needs a value for: {names}. Fill them in on the trigger.
canvas.noFields: This step takes nothing: it just runs.
canvas.unknownHint: The browser does not know "{command}". It is kept as written; edit its arguments in Settings or delete it.
canvas.fieldsHint: A field is a CSS selector, optionally with |@attribute or |html. With Rows set, each field is read inside each row; @href alone reads the row itself.
canvas.onError.continue: Carry on with the next step
canvas.onErrorHint: Leaving the allowed sites always stops the run, whatever this says.
canvas.argsHint: Everything the step carries, including what the form above does not show. Applied when you leave the box.
canvas.argsInvalid: That is not a JSON object, so it was not applied.
canvas.output.none: This step has no output yet. Test the workflow to see what it brings back.
canvas.output.waiting: Waiting for this step to run…
canvas.picker.title: What happens next?
canvas.desc.navigate: Go to an address on one of the browser's allowed sites.
canvas.desc.release: Let go of the run's tab and leave it open where it is.
canvas.desc.click: Click an element with a real pointer, as a person would.
canvas.desc.type: Type into a field, key by key.
canvas.desc.press: Press a key such as Enter or Escape, optionally on an element.
canvas.desc.select: Choose an option in a drop-down.
canvas.desc.scroll: Scroll the page by a distance, or bring an element into view.
canvas.desc.upload: Put a file from the browser's upload folder into a file input.
canvas.desc.wait: Pause for a while, or until an element appears.
canvas.desc.wait_for: Wait until an element is on the page, then go on.
canvas.desc.extract: Read one element's text or attribute, or every match's.
canvas.desc.extract_data: Read named fields into a record, or one record per row of a list.
canvas.desc.screenshot: Keep a picture of the page with the run.
canvas.desc.eval_readonly: Read a value with a short script that cannot change the page.
canvas.desc.push_inbox: File what earlier steps read as messages on a workflow channel (Inbox → Workflow channels). Runs on the server, not in the browser; a re-run never files the same message twice.
canvas.versionsHint: Choose a version to see it on the canvas.
canvas.exec.title: Executions
canvas.exec.hint: Every run of this workflow, newest first.
canvas.exec.noneBody: Test the workflow, run it, or schedule it, and each run shows up here.
canvas.exec.pick: Choose an execution to see it on the canvas.
workflows.title: Workflows
workflows.hint: Build a workflow on the canvas, open one to see it as a graph, and look back at every execution.
workflows.sort.name: Name
workflows.noneBody: Create one on the canvas: open a page, act on it, read what you need.
workflows.exec.noneBody: Runs of saved workflows, from the canvas, a schedule or MCP, show up here.
research.capNoReadNoUrls: Reading a list of pages needs the page reader, which isn't set up on this deployment.
research.urlsHint: One address per line, up to {max}. They're read as given; nothing is searched.
research.lookFor: What to look for in them
research.lookForPlaceholder: e.g. who is hiring engineers, and who raised money
research.urlsInvalid: Give at least one address starting with http:// or https://, and at most {max}.
research.costLine: {queries} search queries · {read} of {tried} pages read · {calls} model calls ({paid} paid) · {tin} tokens in, {tout} out
research.costNote: Usage, not money: this deployment doesn't know what a query or a token costs.
research.evidenceHint: The sentences this run kept, each copied from its page, with the company it names and the signal it reports. Open the source to check it.
research.noEvidence: No evidence was kept from this run.
research.companiesFoundHint: Found in the evidence. Nothing is added to your CRM until someone accepts it on the Companies page.
research.evidenceTabHint: Everything every run kept, searchable together. The same search is the find_evidence tool over MCP.
research.evidenceEmptyBody: Run some research: each run keeps the sentences that matter from the pages it read.
research.budgetHint: Scheduled runs and prospect discovery spend this budget; research someone starts by hand doesn't. At 0, nothing runs on its own.
research.schedulesEmptyBody: Schedule a question or a list of pages, and it runs daily or weekly within the budget.
research.scheduleCreated: Scheduled — the first run starts within a few minutes, if the budget allows
research.scheduleDeleteBody: {name} stops running. The runs it already made, and their evidence, stay.
research.schedulesReadOnly: Managers and above can schedule research and set the budget.
research.schedulesNotConfigured: Neither web search nor a page reader is set up on this deployment, so a schedule would never run. Schedules can't be added here.
research.suggestionsHint: Companies your research found in its evidence. None of them is in your CRM until you accept it.
research.accepted: {name} is in your CRM, with its evidence on the timeline
research.linkedExisting: {name} was already in your CRM: linked, with its evidence on the timeline
research.dismissed: Dismissed — research won't suggest it again
research.suggestionMore: {n} more with weaker evidence — list them with the list_company_suggestions tool.
research.acceptBody: Correct what research read if you need to. The evidence goes onto the company's timeline as a note.
research.noCompanyWrite: Your role can read suggestions but not add companies.
prospects.hint: Companies research found that look like your ideal customer, scored with every point explained. Nothing reaches your CRM until you accept it, and no message is ever sent for you.
prospects.profileHint: What discovery searches for and scores against. Changing it re-ranks the prospects waiting for review.
prospects.offerHint: A sentence or two. The outreach draft uses it as the pitch.
prospects.icpWhoHint: From your CRM's ideal-customer profile, so it's described in one place.
prospects.icpNotConfigured: Not set up yet — discovery is using the defaults. Set it on the ICP settings page.
prospects.queriesHint: One per line; each discovery pass searches the next one. Leave empty to build them from the fields above.
prospects.weightsHint: 0 ignores a signal; 3 counts it three times as much as the default.
prospects.scheduleHint: Runs one search per pass, spending the daily research budget ({used} of {budget} used today).
prospects.profileSaved: Profile saved — waiting prospects were rescored
prospects.notConfigured: Web search isn't set up on this deployment, so discovery can't search. You can still review prospects found before, and edit the profile.
prospects.profileEmpty: Name at least one industry, keyword or search before discovery can run.
prospects.emptyBody: Describe your ideal customer, then run discovery. Each pass searches the web, reads the results and scores the companies it finds.
prospects.contactNone: The pages name no one: write to the team.
prospects.timelineHint: Every piece of evidence, oldest first: the order is the "why now".
prospects.acceptBody: Adds the company, a contact (with an email address) and a deal in your pipeline's first stage, with the evidence on the timeline.
prospects.contactEmailHint: A contact is an address. Leave it empty to add only the company and the deal.
prospects.acceptedNoContact: {name} is in your CRM — company and deal; no contact without an address
prospects.rejectBody: Similar prospects will be ranked lower from now on, and their score will say why.
prospects.draftsHint: A draft to copy and send yourself. Moharrik never sends it.
prospects.draftTemplate: Template — no model is configured, so it's built from the strongest evidence. Edit before sending.
prospects.draftModel: Written by {model} from the evidence only. Check it before sending.
prospects.subject: Subject
prospects.readOnly: Your role can read prospects but not decide them.
prospects.profileReadOnly: Managers and above can change the ideal customer and run discovery.
automation.limits.title: Limits
automation.limits.hint: How much this workspace's automation may do at once, and how long its runs are kept. They apply to every browser and every schedule.
automation.limits.parallelHint: Across all browsers. A run over the limit is refused, not queued.
automation.limits.parallelRange: Runs at once must be a whole number from 1 to 50.
automation.limits.hourlyHint: No site sees one browser more often than this.
automation.limits.hourlyRange: Runs per hour must be a whole number from 1 to 1000.
automation.limits.retentionHint: Older runs, their results and their screenshots are deleted every hour.
automation.limits.retentionRange: Days must be a whole number from 0 to 3650.
automation.limits.adminOnly: Only an admin can change the limits.
automation.sched.kindWorkflowHint: Steps a connected browser carries out, on its allowed sites.
automation.sched.kindJobHint: Work the server does itself, as you, with no browser: collecting sources, syncing Google data, research.
automation.sched.anyBrowserHint: It runs in whichever browser is connected and allows its sites, oldest first.
automation.sched.namedBrowserHint: Only this browser. If it is offline, the run is recorded as waiting.
automation.jobHint.trends.collect: Fetches every enabled source now, within today's budget, like Collect now on the Trends page.
automation.jobHint.google.sync: Syncs every switched-on Analytics property, Search Console site and YouTube channel.
automation.jobHint.research.run: Starts a research run on the topic, as the Research page does.
automation.jobHint.automation.retention: Deletes runs past the workspace's retention now, rather than at the next hourly sweep.
presets.title: Presets
presets.hint: Ready-made browser workflows for the sites a business works on. Add one and it becomes your own workflow: edit it, run it, schedule it.
presets.unknownBrand: There's no such brand in the gallery.
presets.anySite: Opens the address it is given; the browser's allowed sites decide.
presets.addBody: It becomes one of this workspace's workflows, which you can edit, run and schedule.
presets.writesNote: This preset publishes, sends or submits as the account signed in to the site. Every run asks you to confirm first.
presets.whatsappHint: Digits with the country code. Left empty, the number linked on the Inbox page is used. It only ever sends to this number.
presets.profileFilled: Its defaults come from the workspace profile.
presets.profileMissing: Its defaults come from the workspace profile, which has no {fields} yet.

docs.mcp.title: Connect your AI agents to Moharrik
docs.mcp.description: Moharrik is an MCP server. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client can work in your workspace through {count} tools — the CRM, the inbox, campaigns, the notification center, trends, research, browser automation, Google data and the audit log — each limited to the scopes you grant, and never more than your own role.
docs.mcp.connect.title: Connect a client
docs.mcp.connect.intro: There are two ways in. claude.ai and ChatGPT connect by URL and sign you in with OAuth: nothing to paste. Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Cursor send a personal token that starts with mhr_.
docs.mcp.connect.tokenTitle: Get a token (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor)
docs.mcp.connect.tokenIntro: Skip this for claude.ai and ChatGPT: they sign in instead.
docs.mcp.connect.token1: Sign in to Moharrik, or create an account, and open your workspace.
docs.mcp.connect.token2: In the sidebar, under Settings, open MCP tokens and choose Create token.
docs.mcp.connect.token3: Name it after where it will run ("Claude Code on my laptop"), tick only the scopes it needs — see Scopes and roles below — choose when it expires, and create it.
docs.mcp.connect.token4: Copy the token. It starts with mhr_ and is shown only once: if you lose it, revoke it and create another.
docs.mcp.connect.checkPrompt: Use the moharrik whoami tool and tell me my workspace, role and scopes.
docs.mcp.connect.checkAfter: It answers with your workspace, your role and the scopes in effect. If a tool is refused, the answer names the scope it needs: create a token with it, or approve it when you reconnect.
docs.mcp.connect.other: Moharrik speaks MCP over streamable HTTP: JSON-RPC 2.0 posted to the server URL, protocol versions {versions}. Send a token as "Authorization: Bearer mhr_…", or use OAuth 2.1: the server publishes its metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and accepts dynamic client registration.
docs.mcp.scopes.title: Scopes and roles
docs.mcp.scopes.intro: Every tool needs exactly one scope. A token carries only the scopes chosen when it was made; a connected app only the ones approved on the consent page. A call outside them is refused, and the refusal names the scope it needs.
docs.mcp.scopes.roles: Each scope has a lowest role that may hold it. Roles run from owner down to client, and each holds everything below it:
docs.mcp.scopes.shrink: Scopes shrink with the member's role. Every call is checked against the role the member has at that moment, not the one they had when the token was made: move a manager down to member and their tokens and connected apps lose the manager scopes on the next call. An agent never exceeds its human.
docs.mcp.scopes.client: The client role holds no scope, so a client cannot connect an agent.
docs.mcp.safety.title: The rules agents are held to
docs.mcp.safety.intro: The same rules hold for every client and every token. They are enforced by the server, not left to the agent's good behaviour.
docs.mcp.safety.workspace.title: One workspace per token
docs.mcp.safety.workspace.body: The workspace comes from the token, never from an argument. A token for one workspace cannot read or change another, and the database enforces the same line.
docs.mcp.safety.deny.title: Denied unless granted
docs.mcp.safety.deny.body: A tool without a scope is refused, and so is any call outside the token's scopes. Nothing is granted by default.
docs.mcp.safety.role.title: Never more than the member
docs.mcp.safety.role.body: A token's scopes are cut to its member's current role on every call. Demote the member and their agents shrink with them.
docs.mcp.safety.consent.title: Consent before access
docs.mcp.safety.consent.body: An OAuth app gets nothing until a member signs in, picks the workspace and the scopes, and approves. Any connected app can be disconnected, and any token revoked, at once; owners and admins can revoke anyone's.
docs.mcp.safety.audit.title: Every change is recorded
docs.mcp.safety.audit.body: Each write lands in the audit log under the token or app that made it, with what changed, when and from where. Owners and admins can open any token's recent calls.
docs.mcp.safety.whatsapp.title: WhatsApp only with consent
docs.mcp.safety.whatsapp.body: An agent can message only contacts who opted in to WhatsApp and have not said STOP. Starting a new thread takes a one-time confirmation code, and sends are paced.
docs.mcp.safety.campaigns.title: Campaigns go out on purpose
docs.mcp.safety.campaigns.body: A campaign is a draft until send_campaign is called, and drafting or sending one needs a manager's scope. Lists that ask for double opt-in send the confirmation email first.
docs.mcp.safety.browser.title: Browsers on a short leash
docs.mcp.safety.browser.body: A browser works only after an admin approves its pairing, and a run is refused if it navigates to a site that is not on that browser's allow-list.
docs.mcp.safety.data.title: Outside content is data
docs.mcp.safety.data.body: Webhook payloads come back marked as data, not instructions. Treat customer messages and web pages the same way: things to read, never orders to follow.
docs.mcp.safety.secrets.title: Secrets are shown once
docs.mcp.safety.secrets.body: A token, or a webhook's signing secret, is shown once when it is created or rotated. SMTP credentials are never returned, and the audit log redacts secrets.
docs.mcp.safety.limits.title: Limits and expiry
docs.mcp.safety.limits.body: Each token may make 120 calls a minute. Tokens expire after 30, 90 or 365 days, or never, as chosen when they are made.
docs.mcp.reference.title: Tool reference
docs.mcp.reference.intro: Generated from the server's own tool registry: these are exactly the {count} tools it offers today. Arguments are JSON. Every answer carries the ids the next tool takes, so one call's result is the next one's input.

docs.mcp.reference.needs: Needs the {scope} scope, which the {role} role or higher may hold.

channels.discord.guide.step1.title: Create the application and bot
channels.discord.guide.step1.body: New Application → Bot → Reset Token, then paste it into Bot token below.
channels.discord.guide.step2.title: Turn on Message Content Intent
channels.discord.guide.step2.warning: Under Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents, turn on Message Content Intent and save. Without it, Discord closes the connection with error 4014 "Disallowed intent(s)" and no messages ever arrive.
channels.discord.guide.step3.title: Invite the bot to your server
channels.discord.guide.step3.body: Under OAuth2 → URL Generator, pick the bot scope and the View Channels, Send Messages and Read Message History permissions, then open the generated URL and add the bot to your server.
channels.discord.guide.step4.title: Limit it to specific servers (optional)
channels.discord.guide.step4.body: Turn on Developer Mode (User Settings → Advanced), then right-click a server or channel and choose Copy ID. Paste the ids into Allowed servers below — leave it empty to allow every server the bot is in.
channels.discord.guide.step5.title: Test it
channels.discord.guide.step5.body: Send a message in an allowed channel, or message the bot directly — it should appear in the inbox. Use Test connection any time to check the token.
channels.telegram.guide.step1.title: Create the bot
channels.telegram.guide.step1.body: Open @BotFather in Telegram, send /newbot, and choose a name and a username for it.
channels.telegram.guide.step2.title: Copy the bot token
channels.telegram.guide.step2.body: @BotFather replies with a token — copy it into Bot token below.
channels.telegram.guide.step3.title: Let it read every message in a group (optional)
channels.telegram.guide.step3.body: By default a group bot only sees commands and messages that mention it. Message @BotFather with /setprivacy and choose Disable if it should see everything written in the group.
channels.telegram.guide.step4.title: Limit it to specific chats (optional)
channels.telegram.guide.step4.body: Paste the chat or group ids that should reach the bot into Allowed chats below — leave it empty to allow every chat that reaches the bot.
channels.telegram.guide.step5.title: Add it and test
channels.telegram.guide.step5.body: Add the bot to your group, or message it directly, then send a message — it should appear in the inbox. Use Test connection any time to check it.
channels.slack.guide.step1.title: Create the app
channels.slack.guide.step2.title: Add bot scopes
channels.slack.guide.step2.body: Under OAuth & Permissions → Scopes → Bot Token Scopes, add chat:write, channels:history, im:history and groups:history — add app_mentions:read too if the bot should react to @mentions.
channels.slack.guide.step3.title: Install and copy the bot token
channels.slack.guide.step3.body: Install to Workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (starts with xoxb-) into Bot token below.
channels.slack.guide.step4.title: Copy the signing secret
channels.slack.guide.step4.body: From Basic Information, copy the Signing Secret into Signing secret below — this is what proves a delivery really came from Slack.
channels.slack.guide.step5.title: Wire up Event Subscriptions
channels.slack.guide.step5.body: Save this connection below, then paste the Request URL shown here into the app's Event Subscriptions page, subscribe to message.channels and message.im, and save — reinstall the app if Slack asks.
channels.slack.guide.step6.title: Invite the bot to channels
channels.slack.guide.step6.body: In Slack, run /invite @yourbot in each channel it should read.
channels.slack.guide.step7.title: Test it
channels.slack.guide.step7.body: Write to the bot from Slack — it should appear in the inbox. Use Test connection any time to check the token.
channels.email.guide.step1.title: Turn on IMAP
channels.email.guide.step1.body: Gmail: Settings → See all settings → Forwarding and POP/IMAP → Enable IMAP → Save changes. Outlook and Microsoft 365 already have IMAP on by default.
channels.email.guide.step2.title: Get an app password if your provider needs one
channels.email.guide.step2.body: Gmail and Google Workspace: turn on 2-Step Verification, then create an app password and use it below instead of your normal password. Outlook and Microsoft 365 work the same way, usually under Security → Advanced security options.
channels.email.guide.step3.title: Fill in the server details below
channels.email.guide.step3.body: Gmail: imap.gmail.com:993 (TLS) to receive, smtp.gmail.com:465 (TLS) or 587 (STARTTLS) to send. Outlook / Microsoft 365: outlook.office365.com:993 (TLS) and smtp.office365.com:587 (STARTTLS).
channels.email.guide.step4.title: Only recent mail is imported
channels.email.guide.step4.warning: Connecting a mailbox only brings in mail from here on — messages already sitting in it before you connect will not appear in the inbox.
channels.email.guide.step5.title: Test it
channels.email.guide.step5.body: Save the mailbox, then use Test connection to confirm both the incoming and outgoing settings work.
channels.whatsapp.guide.step1.title: Start linking
channels.whatsapp.guide.step1.body: Click Link a number below — or Link with a phone number instead to get a pairing code instead of scanning.
channels.whatsapp.guide.step2.title: Scan it on your phone
channels.whatsapp.guide.step2.body: On the phone: WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device, then scan the QR code shown here — or type the pairing code if you linked by number instead.
channels.whatsapp.guide.step3.title: Keep the phone online
channels.whatsapp.guide.step3.warning: The phone needs an internet connection during this first link. If it goes offline before pairing finishes, the link fails and you'll need to start again.
channels.whatsapp.guide.step4.title: Test it
channels.whatsapp.guide.step4.body: Send a message to that WhatsApp number from another phone — it should appear in the inbox.
channels.chat.setupTitle: Add a chat widget to your site
channels.chat.guide.step1.title: Create the widget
channels.chat.guide.step1.body: Name it and add your site's origin (e.g. https://example.com) to Allowed origins below, then create it.
channels.chat.guide.step2.title: Copy the embed snippet
channels.chat.guide.step2.body: Open the widget's settings (Edit) and copy its embed snippet.
channels.chat.guide.step3.title: Add it to your site
channels.chat.guide.step3.body: Paste the snippet into your site's HTML, just before </body>.
channels.chat.guide.step4.title: Test it
channels.chat.guide.step4.body: Open your site and send yourself a message through the widget — it should appear in the inbox.
channels.workflow.guide.step1.title: Build the reading workflow
channels.workflow.guide.step1.body: In Automation → Workflows, build one on the read preset for this network, ending with a Push to inbox step.
channels.workflow.guide.step2.title: Point this channel at it
channels.workflow.guide.step2.body: Add this channel below and choose that workflow.
channels.workflow.guide.step3.title: Schedule it
channels.workflow.guide.step3.body: In Automation → Schedules, schedule the workflow to run on its own — each run only pushes messages it has not pushed before.
